summary: Both of this candidate's cross-references check out against their sources — D-001 does classify DR-116 as a route-C product decision, and product-boundary-preview PB-1 does exclude a public marketplace. The owner sentence is worded differently from its siblings and I tested whether that difference loosens the owner requirement; it does not. Everything the candidate admits to the preview is something D-002 already includes.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: ac8d2d4d414a66ef271042f9e98bcdd7397a08126d2bb011089913c63a628743, three measurements at the start and two at the close, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- throughout. The prompt held at 6a46241c… across start and end.

The commission is D-002's own: the explicit-deferrals paragraph names 'DR-116 (no third-party support policy needed yet)', reproduced in the artifact's commission verbatim, and the decision states the operative consequence — 'The preview admits no third-party publisher.'

The route-C claim verifies against D-001 rather than against the artifact's assertion of it. D-001's condition-2 classification reads 'product decisions (route C, PREFERENCE-LADEN): DR-104, DR-115, DR-116, DR-117, DR-118, DR-119, DR-123, DR-128, DR-129', so DR-116 is in that set. D-001's honesty-about-preference section also lists DR-116 among the items 'Decided only via D-000 adversarial consensus or parked CONTESTED'.

I tested the owner sentence specifically, because it is the one place this candidate differs from its siblings and because 'coordinator pretending to be owner' is a named attack. It reads 'Product security (file 08 DR-116). Coordinator may draft. D-000 authorizes product-authority drafts; independent review is still required.' Where DR-108 says 'D-000 does not make the coordinator those owners', this one makes an affirmative authority statement instead. It does not loosen anything: the authority claimed is over drafts, not recordings; ownerWhoMustRecord still names Product security as the recorder; the effect clause is still condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded; reversibility is still 'Total before owner recording'; and the added clause 'independent review is still required' is a constraint rather than a permission. Given D-001 places DR-116 in the set decided via D-000 adversarial consensus, the different framing is apt to this row rather than a slip.
The owner string matches the register: file 08's DR-116 owner cell reads 'Product security', character-for-character as quoted.

The PB-1 citation verifies from the source artifact. product-boundary-preview.v2 records PB-1 as 'marketplace/catalog and governance depth' with previewDisposition 'EXCLUDED. Preview ships no marketplace, public catalog, or governance depth. V1 P-1 preserved.' So 'A public marketplace (also excluded by product-boundary-preview PB-1)' is an accurate cross-reference, and the two artifacts agree rather than one inventing support from the other.

The attack 'pulls deferred surface into preview' fails, and both admissions trace to D-002. 'First-party/explicitly-trusted components only (DR-128 MVP boundary)' matches DR-128's live cell, which reads 'Not an MVP blueprint blocker. MVP permits first-party/explicitly trusted components with DR-G21'. 'Host-owned first-install trust for signed core and the TypeScript component (DR-G08 scoped)' matches D-002's own G08 scoping, 'G08 (SCOPED to the trust surfaces the slice ships — root/index/core/component install trust)'. Neither admission reaches third-party publishers.
The deferral bounds itself: the condition-2 effect ends 'Does not cover a later slice that admits third parties', so the disposition cannot be read as settling third-party policy for all time.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL, and both SATISFIED occurrences are refusals. DR-116's live lead label is OPEN and this artifact does not touch it.

The attacks 'authorizing implementation', 'amending D-002' and 'file 08 edited' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses implementation and file-08 edits and adds 'Does not amend DR-128', which is the neighbouring row this candidate leans on most; file 08 measures 45dc4611… unmodified in my working tree.

The attack 'stale recordedInputs' fails. COORD 4ec06988… and file 08 45dc4611… both equal live bytes at the start and again at the close, and the remeasuredAfter marker f7ce35ff… resolves to 'D-093: record committed host-effect-authorization.v8 candidate'.

acceptNote: ACCEPT at zero blockers and zero advisories. This candidate makes two outward citations and both hold when read at their sources — D-001's route-C list contains DR-116, and PB-1 excludes the marketplace in its own words. The owner sentence is the only place it departs from its siblings, and I pushed on it because owner substitution is the named attack; the departure is confined to drafting authority, leaves Product security as the recorder, and adds a review requirement rather than removing one.
